chapters.title: Python, data and mathematics
chapters.definition: A tensor is an indexed collection of numbers; shape lists axis lengths.
chapters.python:
x=[2,3]
w=[4,-1]
z=sum(a*b for a,b in zip(x,w))+1
assert z == 6
chapters.visual: Trace array creation and draw each multiply before summing.
chapters.mistake: Confusing list concatenation with numerical addition.
chapters.question: Predict the dot product when the first input doubles.
chapters.project: Compute mean and dot products without a framework.

chapters.title: AI, ML and evaluation
chapters.definition: A held-out test estimates performance on unseen data from its sampling setting.
chapters.example: TP=3, FP=1, FN=2: precision=.75, recall=.6, F1=2/3.
chapters.visual: Move a threshold and see four labeled confusion cells.
chapters.mistake: Scaling the whole dataset before splitting leaks information.
chapters.question: What is recall when TP=3 and FN=2?
chapters.project: Compare a baseline and threshold model on a held-out synthetic split.

chapters.title: Neurons and activations
chapters.definition: Weights scale inputs; bias shifts the activation threshold.
chapters.example: x=[1,2], w=[2,-3], b=1: z=-3 and ReLU output=0.
chapters.visual: Separate blue inputs, violet weights and aqua activations; show numeric labels.
chapters.mistake: Treating softmax as independent scalar sigmoid.
chapters.question: What does bias=5 produce for the same inputs?
chapters.project: Build AND/OR gates and explain why one perceptron fails XOR.

chapters.title: Tensors and computation
chapters.definition: Rank counts axes; element count is the product of shape dimensions.
chapters.example: A 2 by 3 float32 array has rank 2 and 24 payload bytes.
chapters.python:
import numpy as np
x=np.array([[1,2,3],[4,5,6]],dtype=np.float32)
assert x.shape==(2,3) and x.nbytes==24
chapters.visual: Highlight executed lines and inspect shape, dtype, values and measured nbytes.
chapters.mistake: Calling payload bytes total process memory.
chapters.question: How many payload bytes for shape (4,3), float64?
chapters.answer: 96 bytes, excluding Python object and runtime overhead.
chapters.project: Build a shape inspector and debug incompatible broadcasting.

chapters.title: Forward propagation
chapters.definition: A forward pass applies layers to obtain predictions.
chapters.python:
x=[1,2]
w=[3,4]
z=sum(a*b for a,b in zip(x,w))+1
assert z==12
chapters.visual: Advance contribution, sum, bias, activation and output stages.
chapters.mistake: Transposing weights inconsistently between code and diagram.
chapters.question: What shape does (5,3) @ (3,2) produce?
chapters.project: Verify a 2-to-2-to-1 network by hand and with the existing engine.

chapters.title: Loss and optimization
chapters.definition: A loss measures error; an optimizer changes parameters using gradients.
chapters.example: L=w^2, w=2, lr=.1: gradient=4; next w=1.6 and loss=2.56.
chapters.visual: Draw a loss curve with tangent and editable update arrows.
chapters.mistake: Taking a step in the gradient direction.
chapters.question: For w=-2 and lr=.1, what is next w?
chapters.project: Compare stable, oscillating and divergent step sizes.

chapters.title: Backpropagation
chapters.definition: Backpropagation reuses local derivatives to compute parameter gradients.
chapters.visual: Follow backward arrows with derivative factors and numerical gradient checks.
chapters.mistake: Replacing a derivative with its activation value.
chapters.question: What is dL/dw when x=0?
chapters.answer: 0 for this model; the prediction does not depend on w.
chapters.project: Independently check every dense-network parameter by central differences.

chapters.title: Training and generalization
chapters.definition: Training error alone does not establish generalization.
chapters.visual: Compare training and validation curves and inspect batches.
chapters.question: Does lower train loss guarantee better test performance?
chapters.answer: No; overfitting and distribution changes can reduce test performance.
chapters.project: Train a small model, save its checkpoint and explain a validation gap.

chapters.title: Convolution operations
chapters.definition: A convolution layer shares a filter across spatial positions.
chapters.example: n=5, k=3, p=0, s=1, d=1 gives output length 3.
chapters.visual: Drag a kernel and show aligned products and output cells.
chapters.question: What output length with n=5,k=3,p=1,s=1?
chapters.project: Implement a tiny 2D cross-correlation and compare a framework result.

chapters.title: Computer vision
chapters.definition: Different vision tasks require different labels and metrics.
chapters.visual: Compare class, bounding box and pixel-mask outputs on one image.
chapters.mistake: Using training augmentations on test images without a defined protocol.
chapters.question: Is classification accuracy enough to evaluate segmentation?
chapters.answer: No; assess pixel/region metrics such as IoU and class-wise performance.
chapters.project: Compare frozen-feature and fine-tuned models under the same split.

chapters.title: Sequences and RNNs
chapters.definition: A recurrent state carries information across ordered steps.
chapters.example: For a linear teaching recurrence h_t=x_t+.5*h_previous, [2,2] gives [2,3].
chapters.python:
h=0
for x in [2,2]:
    h=x+0.5*h
assert h==3
chapters.visual: Unroll two timesteps and link shared weights. Label linear simplification.
chapters.mistake: Randomly splitting future observations into training data.
chapters.question: Why are chronological forecasting splits useful?
chapters.answer: They avoid training on future information when predicting the past.
chapters.project: Forecast a synthetic signal and compare against persistence.

chapters.title: Text representations
chapters.definition: A tokenizer maps text pieces to IDs; embeddings map IDs to learned vectors.
chapters.visual: Inspect text, token boundaries, IDs and embedding rows.
chapters.mistake: Confusing a token ID with a semantic distance.
chapters.question: Does ID 10 imply similarity to ID 11?
chapters.project: Build a tiny vocabulary and investigate unknown words and padding.

chapters.title: Attention and transformers
chapters.definition: Attention forms weighted combinations of value vectors.
chapters.example: Equal scores over values [2,6] give weights [.5,.5] and result 4.
chapters.python:
weights=[.5,.5]
values=[2,6]
assert sum(w*v for w,v in zip(weights,values))==4
chapters.visual: Edit Q/K scores, mask a cell and inspect normalized rows.
chapters.mistake: Assuming attention weights alone explain causality.
chapters.question: What output do equal scores give for values [1,5]?
chapters.project: Implement tiny masked attention and a retrieval evaluation with provenance.

chapters.title: Generative models
chapters.definition: A generative model learns a distribution or a process for producing samples.
chapters.example: alpha=1 retains clean; alpha=0 retains noise.
chapters.python:
from math import sqrt
alpha=1
assert sqrt(alpha)*3+sqrt(1-alpha)*7==3
chapters.visual: Move a noise slider; distinguish a teaching mixture from trained diffusion.
chapters.mistake: Judging sample quality from selected examples alone.
chapters.question: What happens to the clean signal at alpha=0?
chapters.project: Compare reconstruction and generation on a small original dataset.

chapters.title: Advanced architectures and representation learning
chapters.definition: Architectures encode assumptions about relations, sequence, space or decisions.
chapters.visual: Animate labeled graph aggregation and contrast positive/negative pairs.
chapters.mistake: Treating a toy aggregation as a trained GNN.
chapters.question: What must be specified for a node with zero neighbors?
chapters.answer: An explicit convention, such as self-features or zero aggregation.
chapters.project: Reproduce a small graph or contrastive baseline with fixed evaluation.

chapters.title: Efficient training
chapters.definition: Efficiency must be measured against accuracy, hardware and workload.
chapters.example: 1000 float32 weights need 4000 payload bytes; optimizer and activations are extra.
chapters.visual: Show separate parameter, activation, gradient and optimizer memory budgets.
chapters.mistake: Claiming twofold end-to-end speed from halving weight precision.
chapters.question: Does 4000 bytes describe all training memory?
chapters.answer: No; activations, gradients, optimizer state and runtime overhead also count.
chapters.project: Profile a baseline and report quality, latency and peak memory tradeoffs.

chapters.title: Interpretability and responsible AI
chapters.definition: An explanation method is evidence about behavior, not proof of correctness.
chapters.example: Group A: 2/10 errors=.2; group B: 8/10=.8, aggregate=.5.
chapters.visual: Inspect aggregate and subgroup metrics with sample counts.
chapters.question: Can aggregate .5 hide unequal group error rates?
chapters.answer: Yes: .2 and .8 average to .5 for equal sizes.
chapters.project: Write a model card with failure cases and scoped privacy assumptions.

chapters.title: Deployment and MLOps
chapters.definition: Serving must preserve the training-time preprocessing and output contract.
chapters.example: 10 ms preprocessing +20 model +5 postprocessing=35 ms (without queue/network).
chapters.visual: Trace the request pipeline and show measured latency percentiles.
chapters.mistake: Calling a model-only benchmark end-to-end latency.
chapters.question: What components are missing from a model-only latency?
chapters.answer: Pre/postprocessing, queue, network and serialization overhead.
chapters.project: Package a small model with schema checks, monitoring and rollback instructions.

chapters.title: Research and capstones
chapters.definition: A reproduction tests whether a claim survives an explicit experimental protocol.
chapters.example: Scores .82 and .80 differ by .02; this alone does not establish statistical significance.
chapters.visual: Compare seeds, confidence intervals, compute budgets and ablations.
chapters.mistake: Selecting the best test-set run as the reported result.
chapters.question: Does a .02 gain from one seed establish robustness?
chapters.answer: No; evaluate variability and confounders under a controlled protocol.
chapters.project: Reproduce a bounded result and publish code, protocol and negative findings.
